'''Giovanni Forni''' is an Italian [[mathematician]] at the [[University of Maryland]] known for his research in [[dynamical system]]s.

After graduating from the [[University of Bologna]] in 1989,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.personal.psu.edu/axk29/CVBrinprize.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae : Giovanni Forni |publisher=Personal.psu.edu |access-date=2015-07-23 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304212018/http://www.personal.psu.edu/axk29/CVBrinprize.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> he obtained his [[PhD]] in 1993 from [[Princeton University]], under the supervision of [[John Mather (mathematician)|John Mather]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=134756 |title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project - Giovanni Forni |publisher=Genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |date= |access-date=2015-07-23}}</ref>

He was an invited speaker at the 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Beijing.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897 |access-date=2015-10-29 |archive-date=2017-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

For his work on solutions of [[cohomology|cohomological]] equations for flows on surfaces, and on the [[Maxim Kontsevich|Kontsevich]]–[[Anton Zorich|Zorich]] conjecture concerning deviation of [[ergodic theory|ergodic]] averages, he was awarded the 2008 [[Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200806/tx080600715p.pdf |title=Mathematics People |publisher=Ams.org |access-date=2015-07-23}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |publisher=Ams.org |date=2015-04-13 |access-date=2015-07-23}}</ref>
